items.step: Given an operator issued a bootstrap token; When a new node submits a CSR (purpose=NODE_CLIENT) with that token; Then the CA signs a cert stamped O=gimle:nodes, and the token cannot be reused.

items.feature: Operator-approval-gated CSR flow
items.step: Given a human submits a CSR (purpose=OPERATOR_CLIENT) with no client certificate; When submitted; Then it sits pending (202) until an existing operator approves it.

items.feature: Certificate rotation (self-rotation and subject-preserving renewal)
items.step: Given a caller presents its own still-valid cert with a matching-subject rotation CSR; When submitted; Then a new cert is issued for the identical subject; a mismatched subject is rejected 403.

items.feature: Zero-downtime TLS material reload
items.step: Given the control plane's cert is rotated; When reloadTlsMaterial runs; Then the HttpsServer is rebuilt with new key material and a fresh connection succeeds.

items.feature: `/secrets/*` byte-for-byte proxy to Fafnir
items.step: Given a caller has WRITE access to SECRET for tenant T; When PUT /secrets/T/mykey; Then ApiServer authorizes locally, forwards byte-for-byte to Fafnir with the calling principal as an internal claim, and relays the response verbatim.

items.feature: Secrets key rotation trigger (proxied)
items.step: Given several encrypted entries exist; When POST /secrets/rotate-key; Then Fafnir generates a new key, re-encrypts every entry, and every previously-encrypted secret still decrypts.

items.feature: CONFIG/SECRET resource-kind separation on one underlying store
items.step: Given a caller has CONFIG:WRITE but not SECRET:WRITE; When PUT /config/{tenant}/{key} with encrypted=true; Then the write is rejected because it routes authorization through ResourceKind.SECRET.

items.feature: `/artifacts/*` streaming proxy to Andvari
items.step: Given --andvari-endpoint is configured; When a caller with ARTIFACT:WRITE PUTs a jar; Then ApiServer authorizes locally and streams the jar straight through, never buffered whole.

items.feature: Andvari-client multi-endpoint failover with rotation
items.step: Given two configured endpoints, the first unreachable; When a HEAD request is made; Then it transparently retries against the second endpoint.

items.feature: `/logs/*` proxy with Muninn fallback
items.step: Given an instance's owning node is unregistered or unreachable, and Muninn is configured; When a caller requests logs; Then ApiServer falls through to Muninn instead of 404/502.

items.feature: `/metrics-history/*` and `/traces-history/*` Muninn proxy
items.step: Given Muninn is configured; When a caller with LOGS:READ requests /metrics-history/{processKind}/{processId}?since=...; Then the request is proxied to Muninn.

items.feature: Node registration, heartbeat, and assignment-fetch API
items.step: Given a node agent starts up; When it POSTs /nodes/{id}/register then periodically /nodes/{id}/heartbeat; Then the control plane records capacity/observations, usable by GET /nodes/{id}/assignments.

items.feature: Unified `AssignedInstance` wire shape across every workload kind
items.step: Given a node has a mix of assignment kinds; When GET /nodes/{id}/assignments; Then every kind is represented uniformly as AssignedInstance entries.

items.feature: Reserved system-tenant auto-seeding
items.step: Given a fresh control-plane replica starts against an empty store; When it initializes; Then it proposes a Tenant row for RESERVED_SYSTEM_TENANT_ID unless one already exists.

items.feature: Bundled web console static serving
items.step: Given the console/index.html resource is present on the classpath; When ControlPlaneMain starts; Then it serves the bundled SPA at /console with client-side-route fallback.

items.feature: Per-endpoint request metrics instrumentation
items.step: Given a request is made to any registered route; When the handler completes; Then request count/latency/error status are recorded, tagged by endpoint and verb.

items.feature: Deployment/Job/DaemonSet/StatefulSet CRUD manifest API
items.step: Given a valid Deployment manifest YAML; When PUT /deployments/{name}; Then GET returns the round-tripped spec, and DELETE removes it.

items.feature: Per-deployment and per-instance metrics rollup
items.step: Given a deployment has 3 ready instances reporting different request rates; When GET /metrics; Then a per-deployment row with the averaged rates is returned.

items.feature: AES-256-GCM secret value encryption with versioned key IDs
items.step: Given a secret encrypted under key id 3; When decrypted after the ring rotates to key id 5; Then decryption succeeds by looking up key id 3 from the embedded byte.

items.feature: Legacy pre-key-id ciphertext format fallback
items.step: Given a blob encrypted before the version/keyId prefix existed; When decrypt() runs; Then the new-format decode fails GCM verification and falls back to the legacy iv||ciphertext layout under key id 0.

items.feature: Local AES-256 key-file generation and loading
items.step: Given no key file exists; When KeyFileManager.loadOrCreate runs; Then a fresh key is generated, written rw-------, and reused on later loads.

items.feature: Key rotation with full-ring persistence (`KeyFileManager.rotate`)
items.step: Given a ring holding key id 0; When rotate() runs; Then a new key id 1 file is written, .active repointed, key id 0 remains loadable.

items.feature: Key-ring fingerprinting for cross-replica drift detection
items.step: Given two replicas hold identical key material in different map order; When fingerprint() is computed; Then both produce the identical SHA-256 hex digest.

items.feature: Full-key-rotation re-encryption sweep
items.step: Given several tenants have encrypted entries under the old key; When FafnirCrypto.rotate() runs; Then every encrypted entry is re-encrypted under the new key.

items.feature: Versioned secret storage layered over ConfigEntry
items.step: Given a secret key written 3 times; When GET /secrets/{tenant}/{key}/versions; Then versions 1,2,3 are all listed and independently retrievable via ?version=N.

items.feature: Optimistic-write versioned put with narrow-lease serialization
items.step: Given two writers race to PUT the same key; When both complete; Then exactly one version number is claimed by each, serialized via a narrow lease around the final @meta-advance step.

items.feature: Soft delete vs hard delete (`?destroy=true`)
items.step: Given a key with 3 versions; When DELETE without ?destroy=true; Then hidden from default GET but every version remains individually readable; with ?destroy=true, every version is permanently removed.

items.feature: Fafnir's own independent RBAC re-check (defense-in-depth)
items.step: Given a forwarded principal claims access but doesn't actually hold the permission; When Fafnir independently re-checks Authorizer.authorize; Then denied with 403 regardless of the forwarder's decision.

items.feature: Node-tenant-scoped secret reads (`gimle:nodes`)
items.step: Given node-42 has an active assignment for tenant T; When it reads GET /secrets/T/{key}; Then granted; PUT/DELETE, or reading an unassigned tenant, is rejected.

items.feature: Authorization-failure throttling and dual audit logging
items.step: Given a principal repeatedly fails authorization; When the failure count crosses the threshold; Then further requests are throttled with 429+Retry-After.

items.feature: Three-tier principal resolution (forwarded header > peer cert > session cookie)
items.step: Given a request carries both a forwarded header and its own peer cert; When resolvePrincipal runs; Then the forwarded header wins.

items.feature: mTLS HTTP server with dynamic TLS material reload
items.step: Given Fafnir's cert is rotated; When reloadTlsMaterial runs; Then a fresh mTLS connection using the new cert succeeds without restart.

items.feature: Console session login (Fafnir's own operator dashboard)
items.step: Given a valid Account; When logging in via Fafnir's /auth/login; Then a distinct gimle_fafnir_session cookie is issued.

items.feature: Plaintext-mode anonymous session carve-out
items.step: Given plaintext mode with no session cookie and no TLS; When GET /auth/session; Then a synthetic "anonymous: true" principal is returned rather than 401.

items.feature: Bundled web console static serving (Fafnir)
items.step: Given fafnir-console/index.html is on the classpath; When FafnirMain starts; Then the SPA is served at /console.

items.feature: Process status endpoint with key-ring fingerprint
items.step: Given Fafnir has run with one key rotation; When GET /status; Then it returns uptimeSeconds/activeKeyId/secretsKeyRingFingerprint/transportProtocol/tenant list — never a raw key.

items.feature: Muninn metrics/traces shipping
items.step: Given -Dgimle.fafnir.muninnEndpoint is set; When FafnirMain starts; Then a MuninnShipper periodically ships this replica's metrics and traces.

items.feature: Fafnir-metrics observability instrumentation
items.step: Given a real request hits any Fafnir endpoint; When the handler completes; Then FafnirMetrics records it, tagged per-endpoint.

items.feature: JPMS module boundary for gimle-fafnir
items.step: Given module-info.java for com.gimle.fafnir; When compiled/linked; Then only com.gimle.fafnir.secret and com.gimle.fafnir are exported.

items.feature: Immutable, content-addressed artifact store
items.step: Given moduleId:version was never pushed; When pushed with jar bytes X; Then CREATED; re-pushing identical X is IDENTICAL (no-op); re-pushing different Y is CONFLICT (409).

items.feature: Streamed, digest-verified push with atomic commit
items.step: Given a push is streaming when the process is killed; When it restarts; Then no torn file is visible at the coordinate's path — only an orphaned temp file (swept later).

items.feature: Size-limited streaming upload rejection
items.step: Given -Dgimle.andvari.maxArtifactBytes (default 500 MiB); When a push streams past that many bytes; Then aborted with 413 before writing excess bytes.

items.feature: On-disk corruption detection and quarantine
items.step: Given stored jar bytes are corrupted after being written; When a GET re-checks the digest while streaming; Then the request already committed to wire is served, but the coordinate is immediately quarantined and audited.

items.feature: Periodic full-store integrity scrub
items.step: Given -Dgimle.andvari.scrub.enabled=true and a stored jar is silently corrupted; When the scheduled scrub runs; Then the mismatch is detected and reported through the same quarantine/audit path.

items.feature: Version retention sweeping (count and age based)
items.step: Given -Dgimle.andvari.retention.enabled=true with maxVersionsPerModule=10; When a module has 15 versions; Then the 5 oldest-by-push-time versions are retired, dual-audited under a synthetic system principal.

items.feature: Multi-replica peer synchronization (no consensus)
items.step: Given two peer replicas and a jar pushed only to A; When B's periodic sync tick runs; Then B pulls the coordinate from A, verifies the digest, and quarantines on mismatch.

items.feature: Peer-sync conflict detection (irreconcilable divergence)
items.step: Given A and B both committed different bytes under the same coordinate; When B's peer sync attempts to pull from A; Then ArtifactStore.put reports CONFLICT and neither replica's copy is touched.

items.feature: Push/pull/list/delete `/artifacts/*` operational HTTP surface
items.step: Given a jar is pushed via PUT /artifacts/{moduleId}/{version}; When HEAD is called; Then a 200 with X-Gimle-Artifact-Sha256; GET streams the jar; DELETE removes it.

items.feature: Maven-2-shaped `/repository/**` interop surface
items.step: Given a jar is pushed via mvn deploy to /repository/com/gimle/.../provider-1.0.0.jar; When fetched via GET /artifacts/com.gimle.examples.greeter.provider/1.0.0; Then identical bytes are returned.

items.feature: Server-computed checksum sidecars (never trusting client uploads)
items.step: Given a client uploads a .jar.sha256 sidecar with an incorrect value; When another client GETs it; Then the response is always the server's own re-derived digest.

items.feature: Generated `maven-metadata.xml` (never stored, always fresh)
items.step: Given three versions pushed out of order; When GET .../maven-metadata.xml; Then the document lists every version in semver order and names the correct latest/release.

items.feature: Maven GAV coordinate translation
items.step: Given com/gimle/examples/greeter/provider/1.0.0/provider-1.0.0.jar; When MavenCoordinates.parseArtifactFile parses it; Then it resolves to module com.gimle.examples.greeter.provider, artifactId provider, version 1.0.0.

items.feature: Defense-in-depth authorization (independent re-check, `ResourceKind.ARTIFACT`)
items.step: Given a forwarded principal claims artifact access but doesn't hold ARTIFACT:WRITE; When Andvari independently re-checks; Then the push is rejected with 403.

items.feature: Module-scoped permission grants
items.step: Given a principal holds a permission scoped to only module com.example.foo; When it pushes/pulls that module; Then granted; catalog listing (whole registry) is denied.

items.feature: Node pull-only artifact access, scoped to active assignments
items.step: Given node-42 holds an active assignment for module M:1.0.0; When it GETs /artifacts/M/1.0.0; Then granted; an unassigned coordinate, or any PUT/DELETE, is rejected.

items.feature: Dual audit logging for push/delete decisions
items.step: Given a push or delete is attempted; When authorizeArtifacts completes; Then a SLF4J line and a durable AuditEvent are both recorded — reads (pulls) are not durably audited.

items.feature: Andvari's own console session story (`/auth/*`, bundled SPA)
items.step: Given a valid Account exists; When logging in via Andvari's /auth/login; Then a distinct gimle_andvari_session cookie is issued and the bundled SPA is served at /console.

items.feature: mTLS server with dynamic TLS reload
items.step: Given Andvari's cert is rotated; When reloadTlsMaterial runs; Then a fresh mTLS connection succeeds without restart.

items.feature: Plaintext-mode loud supply-chain warning
items.step: Given gimle.transport.protocol=plaintext (default); When AndvariMain starts; Then it logs a warning naming that anyone reaching the port can push executable jars.

items.feature: Andvari observability instrumentation and Muninn shipping
items.step: Given a real request hits any Andvari endpoint; When the handler completes; Then AndvariMetrics records it per-endpoint.

items.feature: Process status endpoint (no RBAC gate)
items.step: Given Andvari is running; When GET /status; Then process-level status is returned with no RBAC check.

items.feature: Node platform-log ingest
items.step: Given a running MuninnServer in plaintext mode When a client POSTs a valid NDJSON batch to /ingest/logs/nodes/{nodeId}/{category} Then the response is 200 with the count of appended lines And each line becomes readable back from /logs/nodes/{nodeId}/{category}

items.feature: Instance-log ingest
items.step: Given a running MuninnServer When a client POSTs an NDJSON batch to /ingest/logs/instances/{deploymentName}/{instanceIndex}/{category} Then the response is 200 And the lines are readable back from /logs/instances/{deploymentName}/{instanceIndex}/{category}

items.feature: Node/instance log read with cursor paging
items.step: Given logs previously ingested for a nodeId/category When a client issues GET /logs/nodes/{nodeId}/{category}?cursor=...&limit=... Then the response returns up to `limit` lines older than `cursor`, oldest-first And includes olderCursor/newerCursor for continued paging

items.feature: `follow=true` rejection on Muninn reads
items.step: Given a running MuninnServer When a client requests GET /logs/nodes/{nodeId}/{category}?follow=true Then the response is 400 explaining Muninn only serves shipped history

items.feature: Metrics ingest
items.step: Given a running MuninnServer When a client POSTs an NDJSON batch of counter/timer lines to /ingest/metrics/{processKind}/{processId} Then the response is 200 And the measurements (including percentiles, when present) round-trip exactly on read

items.feature: Metrics read
items.step: same shape as #3, scoped to `/metrics/{processKind}/{processId}`

items.feature: Traces ingest
items.step: Given a running MuninnServer When a client POSTs an NDJSON batch of span lines to /ingest/traces/{processKind}/{processId} Then the response is 200 And span fields (traceId, spanId, name, custom attributes like http.method) round-trip on read

items.feature: Traces read
items.step: Given a running MuninnServer and traces previously ingested for a processKind/processId, When a client issues GET /traces/{processKind}/{processId}?cursor=...&limit=..., Then the response returns matching span lines, oldest-first, with paging cursors (the same shape as the node/instance log and metrics read endpoints).

items.feature: Day-bucketed JSON-lines store with oldest-first cursor semantics
items.step: Given lines timestamped across two different UTC calendar days When they are appended to the same subtree Then two separate day files are created And a late-arriving (out-of-order) line appends into the correct existing day file And a subsequent read returns all lines sorted oldest-first regardless of append/arrival order

items.feature: All-or-nothing batch validation on ingest
items.step: Given a batch containing one valid line and one line missing "timestamp" When the batch is appended Then the whole append throws IllegalArgumentException And nothing from the batch is written to disk

items.feature: Windows-safe on-disk path sanitization for colon-bearing processId
items.step: Given a subtreePath containing a literal colon (e.g. "metrics/CONTROLPLANE/127.0.0.1:8080") When lines are appended and then read back Then the write succeeds by substituting "_" for ":" in the on-disk directory name only And the returned data's processId (from the URL, never the directory name) is unchanged

items.feature: Path-segment validation / directory-traversal defense
items.step: Given a request path with a segment like "..%2F..%2Fetc" When it is decoded and matched against PATH_SEGMENT Then the request is rejected with 400 before any filesystem access happens

items.feature: Age-based retention sweep
items.step: Given a day file older than the configured retentionDays When the retention sweep runs Then that file is deleted And a day file within the window is left untouched And sweeping twice, or sweeping a data root that doesn't exist yet, is a safe no-op

items.feature: Plaintext-default transport with loud unauthenticated-mode warning
items.step: Given gimle.transport.protocol is unset When MuninnMain starts Then MuninnServer binds a plain HttpServer And a WARN log line states every /ingest/* and read call is unauthenticated

items.feature: mTLS transport mode
items.step: Given gimle.transport.protocol=tls and valid cert/key/CA files When a client with a CA-signed leaf certificate connects Then the HTTPS request succeeds and reports transportProtocol=TLS

items.feature: Zero-downtime TLS material reload on certificate rotation
items.step: Given a running MuninnServer in TLS mode with an established client connection When the certificate/key files are overwritten and reloadTlsMaterial() is called Then a brand-new connection at the same port succeeds against the reloaded listener

items.feature: Node-identity check on node-log ingest
items.step: Given TLS mode and a client certificate with CN "node-x" When it POSTs to /ingest/logs/nodes/node-y/PLATFORM Then the request is rejected 403 (certificate identity does not match nodeId)

items.feature: Instance-owner check on instance-log ingest
items.step: Given TLS mode and StoreClient.listAssignments() has no assignment matching (deploymentName, instanceIndex, callerNodeId) When the caller POSTs to /ingest/logs/instances/{deploymentName}/{instanceIndex}/{category} Then the request is rejected 403

items.feature: Verified-certificate-presence check on metrics/traces ingest
items.step: Given TLS mode When a request to /ingest/metrics/{processKind}/{processId} arrives with no verifiable peer certificate Then it is rejected 403 ("no verified client certificate")

items.feature: Read surface has no RBAC/authorization re-check (documented-vs-actual gap)
items.step: Given a running MuninnServer (plaintext or TLS) When any client issues GET /logs/nodes/{nodeId}/{category} (or /metrics/*, /traces/*, /logs/instances/*) Then the request is served with no principal/authorization check of any kind

items.feature: `/status` operational endpoint
items.step: Given a running MuninnServer When GET /status is issued Then it returns 200 with uptimeSeconds and transportProtocol And a non-GET method is rejected with 405

items.feature: Default OpenTelemetry tracer installation
items.step: Given no tracer provider has been installed yet in this JVM When GimleTracing.installDefault() is called (even multiple times) Then a working SdkTracerProvider using LoggingSpanExporter/SimpleSpanProcessor is installed exactly once And GlobalOpenTelemetry exposes it

items.feature: Configurable, batched span exporter installation
items.step: Given a custom SpanExporter (e.g. a capturing test double or MuninnSpanExporter) When GimleTracing.install(exporter) is called Then a real span created afterward reaches that exporter

items.feature: Bounded-wait tracer flush
items.step: Given a tracer installed with a BatchSpanProcessor and a pending unexported span When GimleTracing.flush() is called Then the span is exported before the call returns (bounded to 2 seconds) And calling flush() before any install is a no-op

items.feature: Periodic log-file shipping to Muninn
items.step: Given an active log file with new lines since the last shipped cursor When a shipping tick runs and Muninn accepts the batch (2xx) Then the cursor advances to the last shipped line's timestamp But when the POST fails, the cursor does not advance, and the same lines are retried next tick

items.feature: Periodic Micrometer metrics shipping
items.step: Given a MeterRegistry with counters/timers When a metrics shipping tick fires Then one NDJSON line per meter is POSTed to Muninn's /ingest/metrics/* path

items.feature: One-shot trace-batch and prepared-batch shipping
items.step: Given a list of span lines, or a pre-serialized NDJSON body When shipTraceBatch(...)/shipPreparedBatch(...) is called Then exactly one immediate POST is made per configured endpoint, with no periodic ticker started And an empty batch/body is a no-op (no POST made)

items.feature: Multi-endpoint best-effort fan-out shipping
items.step: Given two configured Muninn endpoints, one of which is down When a batch is shipped Then the batch still lands on the reachable endpoint And the tick is considered successful (cursor advances) because at least one endpoint accepted it

items.feature: In-memory (non-persisted) log-shipping cursor
items.step: (documented tradeoff, not directly assertion-tested as a restart scenario)

items.feature: Micrometer meter → NDJSON codec
items.step: Given a registry with a Counter, a Gauge, and a Timer built with publishPercentiles When MeterSnapshotCodec.toNdjson(registry) is called Then each meter becomes one JSON line with name/type/tags/measurements And the Timer's line additionally carries a "percentiles" map And a Timer without percentiles configured omits the "percentiles" key entirely

items.feature: OpenTelemetry span → NDJSON codec
items.step: Given a batch of SpanData with custom attributes (e.g. http.method) When SpanLineCodec.toNdjson(spans) is called Then each span becomes one line with timestamp/traceId/spanId/parentSpanId/name/kind/status And every span attribute is flattened directly onto that same line

items.feature: `MuninnSpanExporter` (OpenTelemetry SDK integration)
items.step: Given a MuninnSpanExporter wrapping a MuninnShipper pointed at a real ingest stub When export(spans) is called Then the spans reach the stub's /ingest/traces/* endpoint with the expected shape And export() always returns CompletableResultCode.ofSuccess(), even when shipping throws

items.feature: JFR-based per-module CPU/allocation attribution
items.step: Given a module registered under a thread-name prefix "gimle-<module>-<version>-" When a JFR jdk.ExecutionSample/jdk.ThreadAllocationStatistics event fires on a thread with that prefix Then gimle.module.cpu.samples / gimle.module.allocated.bytes counters are incremented tagged by module_prefix And events from unregistered/unclassifiable threads are ignored And JFR being unavailable degrades to "no samples" rather than failing the worker

items.feature: Per-process tagged Micrometer metrics wrappers
items.step: Given a fresh metrics wrapper (e.g. ApiServerMetrics) with an in-memory SimpleMeterRegistry When recordRequest(endpoint, verb, latency, error=true) is called Then the latency Timer, the count Counter, and the errors Counter are all incremented/recorded And requestCount/errorCount return 0 for a tag combination never recorded And different endpoint/verb (or ModuleId, or rpcKind) combinations are tracked independently

items.feature: WorkerMetrics thread-count / metaspace gauges
items.step: Given WorkerMetrics.recordThreadCount(moduleId, 5) then recordThreadCount(moduleId, 9) When the gauge is read Then it reflects 9 (the latest value), not the first recorded value

items.feature: Fafnir authz-failure counter (rate-limiting signal)
items.step: Given a FafnirMetrics instance When recordAuthzFailure("GET") is called Then gimle.fafnir.authz.failures{verb=GET} increments And authzFailureCount for an unrecorded verb returns 0

items.feature: Muninn endpoint list parsing from config
items.step: Given a config value of "host1:9090, host2:9090,,host3:9090" When MuninnShipper.parseEndpoints(value) is called Then it returns ["host1:9090", "host2:9090", "host3:9090"], trimmed and blanks dropped And a null/blank value returns an empty list

items.feature: Fabric-route HTTP-to-service dispatch
items.step: Given a FabricRoute "/greet" bound to interface Greeter, version 1, method "greet", ParamType.STRING When a POST /greet request arrives with body "Gimlé" Then ModuleContext#invokeServiceByName is called with the coerced argument And the response is 200 with the real return value as plain text

items.feature: Fabric-route argument coercion (`ParamType`)
items.step: Given a FabricRoute with ParamType.INT When a request body that isn't a valid integer is POSTed Then the response is 400 with a message naming the expected type And a NONE-typed route is only ever served on GET; every other type is served on POST

items.feature: Vessel-route HTTP reverse-proxy dispatch
items.step: Given a VesselRoute "/api/orders" -> deployment "orders-service", port "HTTP_PORT" When a PUT /api/orders request with a JSON body arrives Then a resolved live instance receives the same method, path, and body unchanged And the gateway's response is exactly that instance's status and body

items.feature: Vessel-endpoint resolution with TTL cache
items.step: Given a resolved endpoint list cached at time T with TTL=5s When resolve() is called again before T+5s Then no new relay call is made (cache hit) When resolve() is called after T+5s Then a fresh relay call is made

items.feature: Round-robin load balancing over ready vessel endpoints
items.step: Given two ready endpoints for a deployment When four consecutive requests are dispatched Then both endpoints are hit, alternating in round-robin order And an endpoint missing the named port or missing a host is never selected

items.feature: Stale-cache fallback on endpoint-refresh failure
items.step: Given a cached endpoint list from a prior successful refresh When the TTL expires and the next refresh returns 504 Then resolve() still returns the previously-cached Ready endpoint, with a warning logged But if no list was ever cached and the refresh fails, resolve() returns Unavailable

items.feature: Vessel-route error surfacing (no ready endpoint / connect failure)
items.step: Given a deployment with zero live/ready endpoints When a vessel route is dispatched Then the response is 503 Given a resolved endpoint that refuses the TCP connection When the proxy call is attempted Then the response is a clean 502, not an uncaught exception

items.feature: Route-table config DSL parsing
items.step: Given a gateway.routes value mixing FABRIC and VESSEL lines, blank lines, and "#" comments When GatewayRouteConfig.parse(text) is called Then blank/comment lines are ignored and each remaining line becomes the correct route type And a malformed line (wrong field count, unknown kind, bad majorVersion/paramType) throws GatewayConfigException naming the line number

items.feature: Duplicate route-path rejection at config-parse time
items.step: Given a config with two lines both declaring path "/api/orders" (one FABRIC, one VESSEL, or same-kind duplicates) When GatewayRouteConfig.parse is called Then it throws GatewayConfigException before any route table is built

items.feature: Gateway HTTP server bootstrap via module lifecycle hooks
items.step: Given required config keys gateway.port and gateway.routes are present When onStart(ctx) runs Then an HttpServer binds on 0.0.0.0:{port}, one context per configured route, using a virtual-thread-per-task executor And onStop() stops the server and flips readiness to false And a missing/non-integer gateway.port throws GatewayConfigException before binding

items.feature: Gateway liveness and readiness probes
items.step: Given GatewayHooks has not yet run onStart Then GatewayReadinessProbe.isReady() returns false When onStart completes successfully (port bound) Then GatewayReadinessProbe.isReady() returns true And GatewayLivenessProbe.isAlive() always returns true

items.feature: HTTP status-code error mapping across the dispatcher
items.step: Given a request to a path with no configured route Then the response is 404 Given a fabric route invoked with the wrong HTTP verb Then the response is 405 Given a downstream fabric call that throws Then the response is 502

items.feature: Boot-only platform-layer JPMS workaround (`requires static`)
items.step: (structural/build-time behavior, not a runtime scenario)

items.feature: Vessel proxy: no TLS, no header forwarding (v1 scope limitation)
items.step: Given a vessel target that reads a custom request header When a request carrying that header is proxied through the gateway Then the header is not forwarded to the target (only method/path/body cross) And the connection to the target is always plain HTTP, never HTTPS

items.feature: Fabric route "quiet success" ambiguity for a misrouted service name
items.step: Given a FabricRoute naming a service interface nothing currently exports When a request is dispatched to that route Then the response is 200 with an empty body (not an error)

items.feature: Deployment resource management (get/apply/delete)
items.step: Given a control plane reachable at --server host:port, When I run "gimle apply -f orders-service.yaml" (kind:Deployment), Then /deployments/<name> is PUT; "gimle get deployments" lists it.

items.feature: Job resource management (get/apply/delete)
items.step: Given a Job manifest (kind:Job), When "gimle apply -f cleanup.yaml", Then /jobs/<name> is PUT; delete then get returns 404/exit 1.

items.feature: CronJob management incl. manual trigger
items.step: Given an applied CronJob "trigger-me", When "gimle cronjob trigger trigger-me", Then prints "cronjob/trigger-me triggered -> job/...-<epochSeconds>"; unknown cronjob fails with exit 1.

items.feature: DaemonSet resource management
items.step: Given a manifest (kind:DaemonSet), When "gimle apply -f node-exporter.yaml", Then /daemonsets/<name> is PUT; no "scale" verb exists (topology-derived, not operator-set).

items.feature: StatefulSet resource management
items.step: Given a manifest (kind:StatefulSet, replicas:3), When "gimle apply -f orders-statefulset.yaml", Then /statefulsets/<name> is PUT.

items.feature: Node inventory and cordon/uncordon
items.step: Given node "node-a" registered, When "gimle cordon node-a", Then POST /nodes/node-a/cordon succeeds and prints "node/node-a cordoned".

items.feature: Instance lifecycle event timeline
items.step: Given deployment "orders-service" index 0, When "gimle events orders-service 0", Then GET /events?deployment=orders-service&instance=0 results are printed. Given an instance with more lifecycle events than --limit, When "gimle events orders-service 0 --limit 5", Then only the 5 most recent events print. Given a tenanted instance's own lifecycle events; When "gimle events <name> <index> --tenant <id>"; Then that tenant's own timeline is printed, and neither the untenanted namespace nor a different tenant's timeline is ever returned in its place.

items.feature: Tenant management and quota configuration
items.step: Given "gimle set tenant acme --max-memory-bytes 1000000000 --max-cpu-millicores 4000 --max-instances 10", Then PUT /tenants/acme is sent; "gimle get tenants" lists "acme".

items.feature: Tenant plain configuration key/value store
items.step: Given tenant "acme" exists, When "gimle set config acme greeting hello", Then PUT /config/acme/greeting; delete then get fails.

items.feature: Versioned secrets management (Fafnir proxy)
items.step: Given "gimle secret set acme db-password --value hunter2", Then base64-encoded PUT to /secrets/acme/db-password; two writes yield 2 versions; "rotate-key" twice increments activeKeyId (1 then 2).

items.feature: Artifact registry client (push/list/get/delete)
items.step: Given "gimle artifact push target/orders-1.0.0.jar", Then the coordinate is read from the jar's own gimle-module.yaml and streamed to PUT /artifacts/<id>/<version>; a second identical push reports "already present".

items.feature: Log viewing and live tailing
items.step: Given "gimle logs instance/orders-service/0", Then GET /logs/instances/orders-service/0?category=APPLICATION&limit=200; "--follow" opens a chunked GET with follow=true and prints new lines until interrupted.

items.feature: Audit trail query
items.step: Given "gimle audit list --principal alice --resource DEPLOYMENT --tenant acme --since 0 --limit 10", Then GET /audit?... is called; "gimle audit" alone prints usage with exit 1.

items.feature: RBAC role management
items.step: Given "gimle set role deployment-reader --permission deployment:read --permission config:write:acme", Then PUT /roles/deployment-reader; deleted role then get returns exit 1.

items.feature: RBAC role binding management
items.step: Given "gimle set rolebinding b1 --subject user:alice --role cluster-admin", Then PUT /rolebindings/b1; "gimle get rolebindings" lists "user:alice".

items.feature: Operator account management
items.step: Given "gimle set account admin --password s3cret-password", Then PUT /accounts/admin sent; JSON output includes "username" but never "passwordHash" or the raw password.

items.feature: Certificate lifecycle management (bootstrap token, CSR request/status/approve, renewal)
items.step: Given "gimle cert request --purpose operator --out-cert op.crt --out-key op.key" against a trust-only connection, Then a keypair/CSR is generated locally, private key written immediately, and CSR POSTed unauthenticated to /bootstrap/csr; a due-for-renewal cred triggers a warning on any other command.

items.feature: Dual table/JSON output formatting
items.step: Given any read verb with "-o json", Then raw JSON printed; default format prints a tab-separated table or "No resources found.".

items.feature: kubectl-shaped global flag parsing, manifest-kind apply dispatch, and mTLS/leader-aware HTTP client
items.step: Given no --server and no GIMLE_SERVER, When any verb runs, Then "no control-plane server configured" and exit 1, no stack trace; a 307 with no Location reports "control plane leader is currently unknown".

items.feature: Topology validation (`hilmir validate`)
items.step: Given a topology declaring zero machines, When "hilmir validate -f topology.yaml", Then a "[ERROR] NO_MACHINES" finding and exit 1; a healthy topology exits 0 (only ERROR-severity affects exit code).

items.feature: Cluster launch planning (`hilmir plan`)
items.step: Given a validated healthy topology with machine "m1", When "hilmir plan -f topology.yaml", Then output includes "machine: m1" and the full StoreMain command line; "--machine m2" filters to just that machine.

items.feature: Real multi-process cluster bring-up (`hilmir up`)
items.step: Given a validated topology, When "hilmir up -f topology.yaml --machine m1", Then every process is spawned in plan order, waited for readiness, remote prerequisites TCP-polled first, and a run ledger written.

items.feature: Cluster teardown and status reporting (`hilmir down`/`status`)
items.step: Given a run ledger from a prior "hilmir up", When "hilmir down --machine m1", Then every process (and descendants) killed in reverse spawn order and the ledger deleted; status against a never-run machine reports a clean error.

items.feature: Cluster TLS/PKI bootstrap (`hilmir pki init`)
items.step: Given an mtls-transport topology with tls.materialDir set, When "hilmir pki init -f topology.yaml", Then a PkiBootstrapMain subprocess writes CA+leaf material; no materialDir fails clearly naming the field.

items.feature: Raft store membership add (`hilmir store add`)
items.step: Given a running store cluster, When "hilmir store add peer-4 host4 9080 9091 --server host1:9091,host2:9091", Then StoreClient#addServer is called with retry and the peer becomes a visible member.

items.feature: Raft store membership remove (`hilmir store remove`)
items.step: Given a previously-added peer, When "hilmir store remove peer-4 --server host1:9091", Then StoreClient#removeServer is called; removing a never-added peer fails fast. Given a cluster grown from three original replicas to four via a prior "hilmir store add", When an ORIGINAL replica (not the one just added) is removed; Then it succeeds and the cluster converges back to three, rather than reporting a misleading "no reachable store leader" for what the leader itself already evaluated and answered.

items.feature: Per-machine platform binary rolling upgrade with quorum-safe store restart (`hilmir upgrade-cluster`)
items.step: Given a machine hosting a store replica among a quorum, When "hilmir upgrade-cluster --machine m1 --new-classpath <cp>", Then only STORE/MUNINN/ANDVARI/FAFNIR/CONTROL_PLANE are restartable (AGENT rejected outright); a store restart is refused if it would break quorum. Given a store replica has been restarted and its port is open again, When the store cluster still cannot serve a leader-routed read, Then upgrade-cluster fails the step rather than reporting it healthy and continuing the rollout.

items.feature: Bundle-based fresh release deployment (`hilmir deploy`)
items.step: Given no existing release "orders", When "hilmir deploy -f orders-bundle.yaml --wait", Then tenant/config/secrets/workloads applied in order, each polled to readiness, revision 1 written; re-deploying an existing release fails clearly.

items.feature: Bundle upgrade with automatic resource pruning (`hilmir upgrade`)
items.step: Given release "orders" rev 1 with workloads A+B, When upgraded with a bundle declaring only A, Then B is pruned, revision 2 written, reported "pruned 1 resource(s)"; no existing release fails clearly.

items.feature: Release rollback to a prior revision (`hilmir rollback`)
items.step: Given release "orders" at rev 3, When "hilmir rollback --release orders" with no --to-revision, Then rev 2's snapshot re-applied as rev 4; explicit --to-revision reads that exact revision.

items.feature: Full release teardown (`hilmir undeploy`)
items.step: Given release "orders" with workloads+tenant, When "hilmir undeploy --release orders", Then workloads deleted reverse-order, tenant deleted, ledger removed; --keep-tenants leaves the tenant.

items.feature: Release listing (`hilmir releases`)
items.step: Given releases exist, When "hilmir releases", Then NAME/REVISION/BUNDLE_VERSION columns listed; empty ledger prints "No releases found.".

items.feature: Release status inspection (`hilmir release-status`)
items.step: Given "hilmir release-status orders", Then bundleVersion/currentRevision/tenants plus each resource's live status printed; a fetch failure shows an "error" field rather than aborting.

items.feature: GitOps directory reconciliation (`hilmir sync`, incl. `--watch` and `--prune`)
items.step: Given 3 bundle files (new, changed, unchanged), When "hilmir sync --dir ./bundles", Then new deployed, changed upgraded+pruned, unchanged reported "already-converged" with zero calls; "--prune" undeploys orphaned releases.

items.feature: `--watch` interval loop for sync
items.step: Given "hilmir sync --dir ./bundles --watch 30", Then the reconcile pass runs every 30s until interrupted.

items.feature: Bundle value templating and override precedence (`${values.*}` substitution)
items.step: Given a bundle with values:{region:us-east}, When rendered with --set region=eu-west, Then eu-west wins; an unresolved reference fails with a named error, never a literal "${values.key}".

items.feature: Bundle manifest schema parsing and validation
items.step: Given an unrecognized top-level key, When parsed, Then GimleManifestException names it; a workload with both file and manifest is rejected as ambiguous.

items.feature: Workload readiness polling for `--wait`
items.step: Given a Deployment applied with --wait, When instances haven't all reported ACTIVE, Then polls every 2s up to a 5-minute timeout.

items.feature: Doctor static deployability diagnostics (`hilmir doctor`)
items.step: Given a jar declaring isolation.tier:TIER_3, When "hilmir doctor my-module.jar", Then TIER3_REQUESTED ERROR and exit 1; a launcher-archive jar under module intent is ERROR, under --vessel INFO.

items.feature: Doctor cluster-aware checks (`--server`, `--tenant`)
items.step: Given a coordinate not present in the registry, When "hilmir doctor my-module.jar --server host:port", Then REGISTRY_COORDINATE_NOT_FOUND (ERROR); an unreachable registry gives REGISTRY_UNREACHABLE (WARNING) instead of a hard failure.

items.feature: Manifest scaffolding (`hilmir init`)
items.step: Given a module-shaped jar with a detected LivenessProbe, When "hilmir init my-module.jar", Then both YAMLs written with the probe class filled confidently; existing deployment.yaml is never overwritten.

items.feature: Gateway extension enable (`hilmir enable gateway`)
items.step: Given gimle-gateway not registered/deployed, When "hilmir enable gateway --server host:port", Then jar pushed and a synthesized bundle deployed fresh; identical-sha jar already registered skips the push; already-deployed at an older version upgrades instead.

items.feature: Gateway extension disable (`hilmir disable gateway`)
items.step: Given gateway currently enabled, When "hilmir disable gateway --server host:port", Then the release is fully undeployed; never-enabled reports a clear "nothing to disable" message.

items.feature: Bundled JRE resolution for platform-binary launches
items.step: Given runtime.useBundledJre:true and GIMLE_HOME set with jre/mimir/bin/java present, When planning a STORE process, Then that exact bundled java path is used; unset GIMLE_HOME fails clearly naming it.

items.feature: `java @argfile` command-line rewriting
items.step: Given a command with many arguments, When JavaArgFile.rewrite is called, Then each argument is individually quoted/escaped into an argfile, and the returned command is [javaExecutable, "@<argfile>"].

items.feature: Run ledger persistence for `up`/`down`/`status`/`upgrade-cluster`
items.step: Given a set of RunRecords written via RunLedger.write, When read back, Then every field round-trips; a corrupt ledger file reports clearly rather than propagating a raw parse exception.

items.feature: TCP-connect readiness polling
items.step: Given a port that never opens, When awaitPortOpen is called with a short timeout, Then times out with a clear message; an already-listening port returns immediately.

items.feature: `mvn gimle:agent` — spawn a real node agent (plus its worker command tail)
items.step: Given "mvn gimle:agent" from gimle-agent, Then a real AgentMain process is spawned with the resolved runtime classpath, plus a worker command tail using gimle-worker's own independently-resolved classpath; run from another module, no-ops.

items.feature: `mvn gimle:bootstrap` — full local-dev cluster orchestration in one foreground command
items.step: Given "mvn gimle:bootstrap" from the root project, Then processes spawn in dependency order, each awaited on its port; by default every gimle-examples module is deployed and awaited ACTIVE (best-effort); "-Dgimle.bootstrap.protocol=tls" runs PkiBootstrapMain first and wires mTLS.

items.feature: Process-launcher Maven goals for individual platform processes (`controlplane`/`store`/`fafnir`/`muninn`/`andvari`/`tls-init`)
items.step: Given "mvn gimle:store" from gimle-mimir, Then StoreMain spawned on raftPort 9080/clientPort 9091; "mvn gimle:controlplane" defaults --store-endpoints to 127.0.0.1:9091 and --fafnir-endpoint to 127.0.0.1:9092.

items.feature: `mvn gimle:deploy` — apply a deployment manifest via a real CLI subprocess
items.step: Given "mvn gimle:deploy -Dgimle.deploy.file=deployment.yaml", Then a real GimleCli "apply -f <file> --server <server>" subprocess is spawned.

items.feature: `mvn gimle:doctor` — run hilmir doctor against the invoking project's own built jar
items.step: Given "mvn gimle:doctor" bound to package phase, Then a real "doctor <jar>" subprocess runs with --vessel/--server/--tenant passed through only when set; a blank server is treated as unset.

items.feature: `mvn gimle:init` — scaffold manifests for the invoking project's own built jar
items.step: Given "mvn gimle:init", Then a real "init <jar> [--out-dir <dir>]" subprocess is spawned; blank outDir treated as unset.

items.feature: `mvn gimle:publish` — push a built module jar to the artifact registry
items.step: Given "mvn gimle:publish", Then a real "artifact push <file> --server <server>" subprocess is spawned using gimle-cli's independently resolved classpath.

items.feature: `mvn gimle:docs` — full documentation site build pipeline
items.step: Given "mvn gimle:docs" from the root project, Then javadoc:aggregate runs, output copied to gimle-docs/static/javadoc, then "bun install"/"bun run build"; missing aggregated output logs a warning without failing.

items.feature: `mvn gimle:flaky-tests` — run known-flaky-tagged tests in isolated standalone reactors
items.step: Given "mvn gimle:flaky-tests" (default modules=gimle-mimir, repeat=1), Then a standalone "mvn -pl gimle-mimir test -Dgroups=flaky ..." child runs; -Dgimle.flakyTests.repeat=0 fails immediately before spawning anything.

items.feature: `mvn gimle:saga` — ensure a Saga test-report server is running
items.step: Given no Saga server listening on 9096, When "mvn gimle:saga", Then a real SagaMain process is spawned detached, pid recorded, health-polled until ready or a 30s timeout; a healthy server is reused.

items.feature: `mvn gimle:verify` — full build run under Saga tracking
items.step: Given "mvn gimle:verify -Dgimle.saga.mavenArgs='clean verify -Psmoke'", Then a run id like "2026-08-17T10-00-00_abc1234" is minted, the child mvn command spawned/streamed, surefire reports swept and imported, run-finished posted; a non-zero child exit fails this build too, only after import.

items.feature: `mvn gimle:saga-import` — standalone sweep-and-import of existing surefire reports
items.step: Given a running Saga server and existing target/surefire-reports/*.xml files, When "mvn gimle:saga-import", Then every discovered report is imported under a freshly-minted or explicit --runId; no reachable server fails immediately.

items.feature: `mvn gimle:saga-stop` — best-effort local Saga server shutdown
items.step: Given a running Saga server, When "mvn gimle:saga-stop", Then POST /api/shutdown called and pidfile deleted; neither present reports "nothing to stop" without failing.

items.feature: Internal — Aether-based cross-module runtime classpath resolution
items.step: Given GimleProcesses.resolveRuntimeClasspath("gimle-worker", version, ...), Then resolves the artifact and its runtime dependencies via Aether; a never-installed artifact throws a clear MojoExecutionException suggesting "mvn install" first.

items.feature: Internal — host-matching java/mvn executable resolution and subprocess supervision
items.step: Given GimleProcesses.javaExecutable(), Then returns the real java binary this Maven process runs under; mavenLauncherUnder(mavenHome) resolves bin/mvn or empty.

items.feature: Internal — git commit/branch capture for run identification
items.step: Given a real git repo, When GitInfo.capture(root) is called, Then real short sha/branch returned; no .git or 10s timeout returns both empty rather than throwing.

items.feature: Internal — surefire report discovery and totals aggregation, including flaky-testcase counting

items.feature: Jobs (run-to-completion workload) list

items.feature: StatefulSets list/detail

items.feature: Instances table with filtering (global + node/tenant-scoped)

items.feature: Cluster metrics charts (lifecycle mix, capacity, quota pressure)

items.feature: Artifact catalog browsing & search

items.feature: Artifact version detail (download, checksum display, delete)
items.step: Given a module has multiple versions, When I select it, Then its versions load on demand; deleting a version calls `DELETE /artifacts/{moduleId}/{version}`.

items.feature: Push artifact dialog (drag-and-drop upload)

items.feature: Maven-2 repository interop view
items.step: Given the console is served at a known origin, When I open `/repository`, Then the repository base URL and a copyable Maven config snippet render.

items.feature: Andvari copy-to-clipboard utility

items.feature: Runs list (no authentication)

items.feature: Live run detail with streaming test feed
items.step: Given a run is LIVE, When I open its detail page, Then new finished-test events are streamed in via NDJSON polling, ending once terminal.

items.feature: Run attachments: Gherkin scenario tree, Chaos ledger, Surtr phase table
items.step: Given a run's events include attachment payloads, When I switch tabs, Then each tab renders its own structured view.

items.feature: Test detail / per-test history
items.step: Given a test has run across several builds, When I open its detail page, Then an outcome strip renders each run's result chronologically.

items.feature: Compare two runs (diff view)
items.step: Given a base/head run selection, When compare loads, Then newly-failing/passing/recovered and >25%-slower tests are each listed.

items.feature: Gjallarhorn flake scoreboard
items.step: Given a 30-day window, When the scoreboard loads, Then entries rank by score descending, quarantined tests are marked, and budget is computed without dividing by zero.

items.feature: Saga console theming (no auth surface)
items.step: Given the console is served, When I navigate to any route, Then no authentication check or redirect occurs.

items.feature: NDJSON event ingest API
items.step: Given a batch with a malformed event on line 3, When I POST it, Then rejected with 400 naming the line number, none persisted.

items.feature: Idempotent per-run ingest / re-ingest replacement
items.step: Given a run already ingested with ledger observations, When re-ingested from scratch, Then its old directory/ledger lines are deleted first and replaced.

items.feature: Crash-safe append (torn-tail recovery)
items.step: Given the last line has no trailing newline (torn write), When a new append occurs, Then the fragment is truncated first.

items.feature: Surefire/Failsafe XML import
items.step: Given a report with a `flakyFailure` element, When imported, Then translated into a failed attempt followed by a passing one; unparseable XML rejected with 400.

items.feature: Fold-import safety net for a live run's gap
items.step: Given a run has live-streamed events for some tests, When I import an XML report for the same runId, Then only test IDs with no `TestFinished` yet are appended, framing never duplicated.

items.feature: Run listing, detail, and cursor-paginated event reads
items.step: Given a run's meta.json is missing or stale, When requested, Then reconstructed on the fly by replaying events.ndjson.

items.feature: Live NDJSON tail (`follow=true`) of a run's event stream
items.step: Given a run is LIVE, When I request `/api/runs/{id}/events?follow=true`, Then new lines stream as appended; the stream closes only after the run reaches terminal AND every line has been delivered.

items.feature: Abandoned-run detection on restart
items.step: Given a run was LIVE when Saga last shut down, When the server restarts, Then that run's status is rewritten to ABANDONED before any read can observe it.

items.feature: Flake ledger derivation (fail-then-pass rule) and rebuild
items.step: Given a test fails attempt 1 and passes attempt 2 in the same run, When the run finishes, Then exactly one flake observation is recorded.

items.feature: Flaky scoreboard with time-window ranking
items.step: Given observations both inside/outside a 30-day window, When I query the scoreboard, Then only in-window observations count.

items.feature: Test-tag index and quarantine status
items.step: Given a test was last observed tagged `flaky`, When I query quarantine status, Then it reports true even if an earlier run tagged it differently.

items.feature: Per-test history endpoint
items.step: Given a test ran in 3 runs with a flaky pass in one, When I request its history, Then each entry reports the final attempt's outcome/duration and flaky flag.

items.feature: Path traversal protection on run IDs
items.step: Given a run ID containing `../` or path separators, When validated, Then rejected with 400.

items.feature: Bundled console static serving
items.step: Given the console jar is bundled, When SagaMain starts, Then `/console` serves the SPA; absent, `/console` is disabled with a log line.

items.feature: Poll-until-condition primitive (`Await`)
items.step: Given a boolean condition and a timeout, When the condition becomes true before the deadline, Then `Await.until` returns immediately; When the deadline passes first, Then it throws naming the condition.

items.feature: Kernel-assigned loopback port leasing (`PortLease`)
items.step: Given a requested port count, When `PortLease.reserve(n)` is called, Then n distinct kernel-assigned loopback ports are bound and held; `release(port)` closes the socket and hands the port number to the process.

items.feature: Heimdall event-driven cluster condition harness
items.step: Given control-plane replica base URLs and supervised processes, When a registered view/log/probe condition's predicate becomes true, Then the corresponding HeimdallCondition future completes; a supervised process dying fails every pending condition immediately.

items.feature: Replica-scoped condition observation
items.step: Given `cluster.when(1)`, When a ClusterView satisfying the predicate is fetched from replica 1, Then the condition completes; views from other replicas are ignored.

items.feature: Deployment/node/log condition builders
items.step: Given a deployment name, When `.isActive()`/`.hasActiveReplicas(n)`/`.allOnVersion(v,n)`/`.hasFailedInstance()`/`.isAbsent()`/`.reportsQuotaViolation()` is awaited, Then it resolves once the corresponding condition holds.

items.feature: Time-windowed negative invariants (`Invariant`/`InvariantGuard`)
items.step: Given an Invariant and a Duration window, When `holdFor(invariant, window)` runs, Then every observed view is checked; the call throws with a forensic report the instant one violates it.

items.feature: Forensic failure reporting
items.step: Given a condition times out or a process dies, When the failure is raised, Then the error message includes the last ClusterView, process liveness, recent harness events, and recent platform events.

items.feature: `hello-module` — minimal inert deployable fixture
items.step: Given the hello-module jar and its deployment.yaml, When deployed with 1 replica, Then it reaches ACTIVE with no health probes or lifecycle hooks resolved (none declared).

items.feature: `greeter-provider` — real fabric service export with lifecycle hooks and health probes
items.step: Given greeter-provider deployed with a tenant, When the instance starts, Then it registers Greeter on the fabric, ReadinessProbe reports ready only after registration, and logs the tenant's secret value fetched via ctx.config(...).

items.feature: `greeter-consumer` — real cross-worker fabric call with MDC-tagged background caller
items.step: Given greeter-consumer deployed alongside greeter-provider, When the consumer's background loop runs, Then every 5s it looks up Greeter, calls greet("Gimlé"), and logs the reply with its own instance's MDC tags applied.

items.feature: `greeter-load-generator` — HTTP bridge for external load tools driving real fabric traffic
items.step: Given greeter-load-generator deployed with load.port via tenant config, When an HTTP GET hits /call, Then it performs a real lookupService(Greeter.class)+greet("Gatling") call and reflects 200/502/503 based on outcome.

items.feature: Real multi-process cluster fixture (store/control-plane/agent/Fafnir/Muninn)
items.step: Given `GreeterSmokeClusterSupport.startCluster()`, When the fixture boots, Then 3 store nodes, 2 control-plane replicas, 1 agent, 2 Fafnir replicas, and 1 Muninn are all live real processes torn down in reverse dependency order.

items.feature: On-the-fly compiled module variants via `TestModuleBuilder`
items.step: Given a variant spec, When `buildFaultyProviderJar()` is called, Then a real compiled jar with that behavior is produced and deployable through the real HTTP API.

items.feature: Base cluster topology deploy across store cluster and multiple CP replicas
items.step: Given a real cluster, When greeter-provider and greeter-consumer are deployed, Then both reach ACTIVE (observed via a different replica than submission), the consumer's fabric call appears in its own log, and the provider's log shows its secret round-tripped through Fafnir.

items.feature: Raft store resilience (member loss, leader failover, live membership change)
items.step: Given a real 3-store cluster with concurrent writes in flight, When a store node (or the leader) is killed, Then the cluster keeps accepting writes and no acknowledged write is lost.

items.feature: Tiered self-healing (worker respawn, liveness-exhaustion escalation to FAILED)
items.step: Given an ACTIVE instance, When its worker JVM is force-killed, Then the agent respawns a new worker and the deployment returns to ACTIVE; a never-recovering module escalates to FAILED after budget exhaustion.

items.feature: Classloader leak detection wired into a real worker
items.step: Given a module leaving a background platform thread running past onStop, When redeployed to a new version, Then a ModuleLeakDetected event is logged to worker-platform.log.

items.feature: Repeated redeploy stability without false-positive leaks
items.step: Given a well-behaved module on a shared Tier 1 worker, When redeployed several times in a row, Then LeakTracker never reports a leak for any cycle.

items.feature: Tier 1 worker density packing and its cap
items.step: Given up to MAX_TIER1_DENSITY distinct Tier 1 modules deployed, When each deploys, Then all pack onto one real worker process; one more distinct module gets a fresh worker.

items.feature: Node cordoning blocks new placement without evicting running instances
items.step: Given a cordoned single-node cluster, When a new deployment is submitted, Then it stays unplaced, while an already-running instance keeps serving.

items.feature: DaemonSet per-node fan-out and dead-node assignment cleanup
items.step: Given a DaemonSet deployed across 2 real agent nodes, When both are up, Then one instance per node; When one node's agent is hard-killed, Then that node's assignment is cleaned up.

items.feature: Job and CronJob real-cluster lifecycle
items.step: Given a Job-kind module returning SUCCEEDED, When deployed, Then it reaches JobPhase.SUCCEEDED; a triggered CronJob generates a Job that likewise succeeds.

items.feature: StatefulSet sticky placement and volume persistence across worker restart
items.step: Given a StatefulSet instance that wrote a marker file, When its worker is killed and respawned, Then the instance lands on the same node and sees the marker file already present.

items.feature: Rolling update preserves serving capacity and reaches new version
items.step: Given a 2-replica deployment with maxUnavailable=1/maxSurge=1, When rolled to v1.1.0, Then at least 1 instance stays ACTIVE throughout and all 2 end on v1.1.0.

items.feature: Surge worker promotion carries out via in-place retarget, not respawn
items.step: Given a 2-replica rollout with maxUnavailable=1/maxSurge=1, When the surge worker is promoted, Then its OS PID is unchanged, while the other (restarted) instance's PID changes.

items.feature: Autoscaling under real request-rate, error-rate, queue-depth, and weighted-blended load
items.step: Given an autoscale policy targeting a signal, When real Gatling-generated load pushes it past target, Then the deployment scales toward maxReplicas.

items.feature: Multi-tenant quota enforcement (flag-not-evict, and admission rejection)
items.step: Given a tenant already running at quota, When quota is lowered, Then the deployment is flagged but keeps running; a new submission exceeding quota is rejected with 409.

items.feature: Circuit breaker excludes a consistently-failing replica
items.step: Given a genuinely broken provider replica hanging past the client timeout, When enough consecutive calls fail via real timeout, Then FabricServiceRegistry's breaker opens and excludes that replica.

items.feature: Gossip/SWIM failure detection across real separate agent processes
items.step: Given real agent processes joined via gossip, When one is hard-killed, Then every surviving agent's SWIM state eventually marks it dead.

items.feature: Observability data survives agent death (Muninn fallback) and control-plane metrics round-trip
items.step: Given a deployed instance logging normally, When its agent dies, Then its log is still readable via the /logs/* Muninn fallback.

items.feature: Worker-tier metrics/trace relay to Muninn via the agent
items.step: Given a real deployed module making a real fabric call, When its worker relays MetricsSnapshot/TracesSnapshot to its agent, Then the agent forwards it to Muninn and it's readable via GET /metrics-history/*.

items.feature: Artifact registry (Andvari) resolution path end to end
items.step: Given a real Andvari replica and a pushed jar, When a coordinate-only deployment is submitted, Then the agent resolves and caches the jar and the instance reaches ACTIVE.

items.feature: External HTTP request reaches a fabric service through the gateway
items.step: Given greeter-provider and gimle-gateway deployed as a DaemonSet on an edge-labeled node, When an external client hits the gateway, Then the response reflects a real fabric call to greeter-provider.

items.feature: Declarative cluster topology DSL/YAML parsing and validation
items.step: Given a topologies/*.yaml file or a ClusterTopology.named(...) DSL chain, When parsed/built, Then a ClusterSpec results; the one unsupported combination (fault-proxied + mTLS) is rejected before any process spawns.

items.feature: Real subprocess cluster orchestration (`GimleCluster`)
items.step: Given a ClusterSpec, When GimleCluster.start(spec, workDir) runs, Then every declared process is a live, correctly-wired real subprocess reachable through cluster.api()/cluster.when().

items.feature: Cluster pooling per topology with destructive-scenario isolation
items.step: Given a scenario tagged @destructive, When it starts, Then a brand-new GimleCluster is booted solely for it; non-destructive scenarios reuse the shared pooled cluster.

items.feature: JUnit `@Holmgang`/`@HolmgangCluster` extension for plain-JUnit cluster tests
items.step: Given a class annotated @Holmgang(topology="...") with a @HolmgangCluster field, When JUnit runs the test, Then the extension boots the topology and injects the cluster.

items.feature: Fenrir randomized chaos-fault soak executor
items.step: Given a FenrirPlan with a soak duration and strike interval, When Fenrir.unleash(cluster, plan) runs, Then it repeatedly draws a fault kind/victim, applies it, and awaits recovery through Heimdall, recording each strike into a ChaosLedger.

items.feature: Chaos ledger recording and rendering
items.step: Given a completed Fenrir run, When its ChaosLedger is queried, Then executedCount()/recoveredCount()/skippedCount()/allRecovered() reflect actual strikes.

items.feature: Randomized fault soak with no lost writes (basic and compound-fault modes)
items.step: Given a running HA cluster and a background write workload, When Fenrir is unleashed striking every 15s, Then at least 3 faults execute, every fault recovers, and every acknowledged write remains readable.

items.feature: Muninn/Andvari replica-bounce resilience soak
items.step: Given a topology with 2 Muninn and 2 Andvari replicas, When Fenrir strikes only Muninn/Andvari bounces, Then at least 2 faults execute and recover, and a coordinate-only deployment still reaches ACTIVE afterward.

items.feature: Live store membership change (AddServer/RemoveServer)
items.step: Given a 3-store HA cluster, When a fourth store node joins, Then the store reports 4 members and accepts writes; leaving reports 3 members again.

items.feature: Mutual TLS end-to-end operation and anonymous-client rejection
items.step: Given an mTLS-transport cluster, When greeter-provider is deployed with a tenant secret, Then it logs the secret value within 60s; an anonymous client attempting a write is rejected with 401.

items.feature: Control-plane partition tolerance (store-side) and reconvergence on heal
items.step: Given a fault-proxied HA cluster, When the network between control plane 1 and all stores is cut, Then control plane 1 stops serving within 30s while a submission via replica 0 still reaches ACTIVE; on heal, also ACTIVE via replica 1.

items.feature: Store leader self-demotion under silent peer partition; bounded write latency
items.step: Given an HA cluster, When the store leader is partitioned, Then it steps down within 10s; a write submitted during the partition completes within 30s (success or failure).

items.feature: Tenant deployment lifecycle with secret delivery and clean deletion
items.step: Given a tenant secret and a deployment submitted, When the instance starts, Then it logs the secret within 60s; on deletion, absent within 60s.

items.feature: Tenant quota retroactive violation (flag, not evict) and admission rejection
items.step: Given a tenant at quota, When quota is lowered, Then the deployment reports a violation within 60s while keeping its 1 ACTIVE instance for 10s; a starved-tenant submission is rejected with 409.

items.feature: Node cordoning blocks placement until uncordoned
items.step: Given node-1 cordoned, When a deployment is submitted, Then it stays unplaced for 10s; uncordoning it, the deployment reaches ACTIVE within 120s.

items.feature: Worker-tier self-healing and liveness-exhaustion escalation (Gherkin coverage)
items.step: Given greeter-provider deployed, When its worker is killed, Then within 120s the deployment is ACTIVE again; an always-failing-liveness provider escalates to a FAILED instance within 240s once its restart budget exhausts.

items.feature: Zero-downtime rolling update under surge budget (Gherkin coverage)
items.step: Given a 2-replica deployment with a guard held, When rolled with maxUnavailable=1/maxSurge=1, Then within 180s both instances are ACTIVE on the new version, and the guard held throughout.

items.feature: Request-rate autoscaling under real Gatling-driven fabric load (Gherkin coverage)
items.step: Given greeter-load-generator deployed and an autoscaling deployment targeting 5 rps min 1/max 2, When 20 rps load runs for 60s, Then within 120s the deployment has 2 ACTIVE replicas.

items.feature: Artifact registry coordinate-only deployment (Gherkin coverage)
items.step: Given a running "registry" topology, When greeter-provider is pushed and a deployment is submitted with no artifact path, Then within 60s the deployment is ACTIVE.

items.feature: Surtr scale/churn/performance workload runner
items.step: Given a SurtrWorkload and its declared topology, When SurtrRunner.run() executes each job in order, Then measurements are collected from real cluster state/event logs and gates evaluated into a SurtrRunResult.

items.feature: Surtr Muninn-window measurement (documented gap)
items.step: Given a workload requesting the muninnWindow measurement, When the run completes, Then it always reports a skipped placeholder series ("Muninn window metrics collection is not implemented in this build").

items.feature: Module-density Tier 1 packing Surtr reference workload
items.step: Given workloads/module-density.yaml (10 iterations at 8 qps against topologies/surtr-density.yaml), When run via SurtrIT, Then all created deployments reach ACTIVE within 180s and the gates pass.

items.feature: Saga unified run reporting (Gherkin + JUnit + Fenrir + Surtr)
items.step: Given a -Pvalidation run, When the JVM shuts down, Then SagaCollector.flush() writes a versioned JSON report plus a self-contained HTML console with that run's data embedded.

items.feature: Saga best-effort shipping to a remote report server
items.step: Given -Dgimle.saga.endpoint=<url>, When the collector flushes, Then it POSTs NDJSON-encoded attachment events; an unset/unreachable/erroring endpoint silently no-ops and never fails the run.

items.feature: Loki fault-injection proxy for store/control-plane link partitions
items.step: Given a fault-proxied topology, When cutControlPlaneFromStores(index) is called, Then that replica's links reset immediately; cutStoreFromPeers(index) blackholes raft traffic until heal().

items.feature: Utgard multi-container distributed boot ordering
items.step: Given a 3-container fleet, When `hilmir up --machine` is issued for the server machine before prerequisites, Then it blocks until store and Fafnir machines are up, then completes and a real deployment reaches ACTIVE.

items.feature: Utgard real machine loss (hard container kill) and rejoin

items.feature: Utgard network partition (vs hard kill) with reconvergence
items.step: Given an instance on one agent machine, When disconnected from the network, Then rescheduled to the surviving machine; reconnecting converges to exactly 1 ACTIVE instance.

items.feature: Utgard real-hostname mTLS bootstrap across containers
items.step: Given two containers with `hilmir pki init` on the server machine, When `hilmir up` runs on each, Then the agent's CSR bootstrap succeeds over mTLS automatically, and the CLI dialing the server's real hostname shows the agent's node.

items.feature: Utgard Docker container fleet management primitives
items.step: Given UtgardMachines.start(names), When a live Docker daemon with registry access is available, Then real containers boot on a shared network; blocked image pulls throw UtgardDockerUnavailableException and dependent tests skip via assumeTrue.

items.feature: Docker Compose manual validation topologies (bundled-JRE and full-JRE)
items.step: Given `mvn -pl gimle-dist -am install -P dist-with-jre` produced the tarball, When `docker compose -f docker-compose.bundled-jre.yml up` runs, Then every service launches off `jre/<component>/bin/java` from a shared volume, with agent alone using a real eclipse-temurin base image.

items.feature: Standalone CLI distribution archive
items.step: Given `mvn -pl gimle-dist package`, When the cli assembly execution runs, Then `gimle-cli-<version>.tar.gz` contains bin/gimle, bin/gimle.cmd, and lib/*.jar scoped to exactly gimle-cli/core/module/pki, slf4j, logback, snakeyaml, Bouncy Castle.

items.feature: Standalone Hilmir bootstrap-tool distribution archive
items.step: Given `mvn -pl gimle-dist package`, When the hilmir assembly execution runs, Then `gimle-hilmir-<version>.tar.gz` contains bin/hilmir, bin/hilmir.cmd, and lib/*.jar scoped to hilmir, core, slf4j, logback, snakeyaml.

items.feature: Cluster-machine platform distribution archive
items.step: Given `mvn -pl gimle-dist package`, When the platform assembly execution runs, Then `gimle-platform-<version>.tar.gz` contains lib/*.jar (full closure minus gateway), modules/gimle-gateway-*.jar (undeployed), and all four wrapper scripts (bin/gimle, bin/gimle.cmd, bin/hilmir, bin/hilmir.cmd).

items.feature: Opt-in bundled-JRE distribution variant (`dist-with-jre` profile)
items.step: Given `mvn -pl gimle-dist -am install -P dist-with-jre`, When the profile's exec-maven-plugin executions run, Then a trimmed JRE (--strip-debug --no-header-files --no-man-pages) is jlinked per component; the three archives additionally contain jre/<component>/ for their own components.

items.feature: Distribution archive checksums and SBOM generation
items.step: Given `mvn -pl gimle-dist package`, When cyclonedx-maven-plugin and maven-antrun-plugin executions run, Then bom.json is generated and copied per archive, and a .sha256 checksum file is written next to each.

items.feature: Norn deterministic virtual-time Raft fault-injection simulation
items.step: Given a 3-node NornCluster wired in-process with a shared virtual TestClock, When 20 seeded fault schedules of 40 rounds each are run — each round randomly isolating a node, restarting a node, healing all nodes, or proposing a state mutation through the current leader — Then Election Safety (at most one leader per term) and Log Matching (agreeing entries at any shared index/term are identical) hold after every single round. Given a seed's 40-round fault storm has just ended, When every node is healed via healAll, Then the cluster eventually elects a leader and commits a fresh proposal within a 10-second virtual-time liveness budget. Given one of the 20 seeds fails a safety or liveness assertion, When the failure is reported, Then it includes that seed's full per-round action ledger so the exact failing schedule reproduces by rerunning only that seed.

items.feature: Service abstraction: stable name, CRUD API, and endpoint reconciliation
items.step: Given a Service "orders" selecting deployment "orders-service" on port 8080, When POSTed to /services and the reconciler ticks against a store with an ACTIVE, ready instance of "orders-service", Then GET /services/orders/endpoints returns that instance's real host:port. Given a Service whose selected deployment currently has no ACTIVE-and-ready instance, When the reconciler ticks, Then it converges to an empty endpoint list rather than failing. Given a Service posted with the same name twice, When the second POST carries a different deploymentNames/port, Then GET returns the second spec, replacing the first entirely.

items.feature: Fabric listener-side tenant re-check on inbound service calls
items.step: Given a module exporting an interface restricted to allowedTenantIds ["tenant-a"], When a caller wire-carrying callerTenantId "tenant-b" dials the ServiceEndpoint's raw address directly (bypassing FabricServiceRegistry's own caller-side filter), Then FabricServer.dispatch independently rejects the call with GimleFabricAuthorizationException. Given the same restricted export, When a caller carrying callerTenantId "tenant-a" dials directly, Then the listener's own re-check permits the call through. Given an export with no allowedTenantIds restriction, When any caller (including an untenanted one) dials directly, Then the call is permitted -- the re-check enforces exactly what the module declared, never a stricter default. Given a module exporting an interface restricted to allowedTenantIds ["tenant-a"] behind a TLS listener, When a caller holding a worker certificate for tenant-b dials it directly and writes callerTenantId "tenant-a" into the frame, Then the listener refuses the call as a claim/certificate mismatch, naming the certified tenant-b. Given the same listener, When a caller holding a tenant-a worker certificate writes no claim at all, Then the call is served under tenant-a, read off the certificate.

items.feature: gimle-bifrost: per-node service proxy (kube-proxy analogue)
items.step: Given BifrostProxy polling a ServiceSource that reports Service "orders" with two live endpoints, When pollOnce runs, Then a loopback listener is bound at a stable 127.x.y.1 address and successive connections round-robin across both endpoints. Given a service previously bound, When it disappears from the next poll's service list, Then its listener is closed. Given a service appearing for the first time on a poll, When pollOnce runs, Then a new listener is bound for it without disturbing already-bound listeners for other services.

items.feature: gimle-skald: cluster DNS server resolving Service names to live endpoints
items.step: Given the directory has never held an entry for a queried name inside the svc.gimle.local zone, When queried, Then the response is NXDOMAIN. Given the directory holds a declared Service whose endpoint list is currently empty, When queried, Then the response is NOERROR with zero answer records rather than NXDOMAIN. Given SkaldServer's directory cache holds "orders.acme.svc.gimle.local" -> [10.0.0.5], When a standard A query for that name arrives over UDP, Then the response carries exactly that one A record. Given a query for a name outside svc.gimle.local, or a non-A query type, or a non-QUERY opcode, When received, Then the response is NOTIMP/NXDOMAIN as appropriate rather than silence.

items.feature: Gateway virtual-host routing and Service-backed (SERVICE) route kind
items.step: Given two routes declared at the same path, one HOST orders.example.com and one host-unconstrained, When a request arrives with Host: orders.example.com, Then the host-constrained route serves it; When a request arrives with a different or missing Host header, Then the host-unconstrained sibling serves it instead. Given a route declared HOST orders.example.com only, When a request arrives with a non-matching Host header, Then the response is 404, not a fallback to any other route at that path. Given a SERVICE route naming a control-plane Service with a live ready endpoint, When dispatched, Then the request is proxied verbatim to that endpoint's host:port, resolved through ServiceEndpointCache's own TTL-bounded relay to GET /services/{name}/endpoints; When the Service has no ready endpoint, Then a clear error status is returned, not a silent 200.

items.feature: Hosted-module runtime port reporting folded into instance observation
items.step: Given a hosted module's onStart hook calls ctx.reportPort(name, port), When the worker's next metrics report reaches its node agent, Then that instance's observation JSON carries the reported port under the same "ports" key shape a Vessel workload's allocatedPorts already uses. Given a module reports exactly one port, When ServiceEndpointResolver resolves a Service fronting that module's deployment, Then solePort() succeeds and a live endpoint is produced -- closing the gap where only Vessel instances could ever resolve.

items.feature: NetworkPolicySpec durable persistence through StoreClient
